title: the ball plays the samba on the rings
story: Magalenha at 117.4 BPM: a thin samba groove whose percussion lands on the 8th-note grid, building (slope 1.77) through an anomaly at 1388 into the full-band drop on the 10.8 onset at 1452 (rms 0.05 -> 0.14). The rings turn slowly and the ball, thrown from the centre at a round start on the grid (ronda 29.03), crosses ring 0 in exactly one beat with no gravity and a perfect bounce, so every wall hit lands on a beat or an off-beat 8th; it flashes on its first hits so the viewer learns the mechanism, then works outward ring by ring as the stops rotate on each bar and the picture brightens.. It reaches the last ring just before the drop; on 1452 the spin reverses, the gaps blow open, the ball is thrown twice as hard (impulso 0.57->1.14) so its wall hits land on the 8th-note grid, and from 1436 the samba batucada is carried bar after bar at 16th resolution: the dark surdo hits punch the zoom and shake hard, the surdo answer pulls the zoom out lightly, the caixa and tamborim strokes give small shakes and the agogo a brightness tick, while the palette sways in hue every half bar.
